property: SLIP and PPP both served serial/dial point-to-point IP access environments, while PPP expanded the role to negotiated multi-protocol links with LCP/NCP and authentication hooks.

date_or_range.notes: Contemporary access servers such as PortMaster supported both SLIP and PPP.

sources.locator: PortMaster Configuration Guide, async SLIP/PPP configuration sections

negative_claims: This edge does not claim PPP is a formal revision of SLIP.
This edge does not claim RFC 1134 cites SLIP as a design ancestor.
Operational displacement of SLIP by PPP must be documented by deployments/product histories rather than inferred solely from feature differences.
open_questions: Recover migration guidance from ISPs/Unix vendors moving SLIP users to PPP.
Trace CSLIP and PPP header-compression branches separately.
notes: A deliberate example where role succession is plausible but direct causal ancestry is not yet asserted.
